notes: Source 4 = Boling 1975 (Tananir = Buildings A and B on the lower slope of Gerizim). s4f1: Welter's 'plastered cistern' in the SW corner room (p. 33) is taken to be Silo A in room 7 at the SW corner of Building A (p. 45; Figs. 2, 13); p. 59 oddly calls Silo A 'the northern "cistern"', but the plans and p. 45 put it in the SW corner. s4f2 position: Building B was found 'one step down the mountainside' (p. 57) beyond the 'northern, downhill, limit' of the field (p. 36), so Silo B lies in the north part of the site; coded N relative to the site. The north arrows of Figs. 2 and 13 point to the upper left, which would put Building B about NNE-NE (c. 30-45 deg) of Building A, but the unit's recorded point (approximate, 100 m precision) cannot be placed on any plan: Figs. 2 and 13 have no coordinates, and the grid lines 13-15 on the Fig. 1 location plan are not tied to the packet grid. So no plan positions. s4f3 is shown only on the plans (room 2), so its position is none. s4f4: two cisterns on the east beside the houses, both called modern; coded as one feature. Not coded: the area 9 rock-cut 'vat' with a settling depression, NW of the main building, probably Roman-Byzantine (pp. 40-41) - PROTOCOL excludes vats from pools, and it is not a cistern or pit; the area 8 circular enclosure; the spring. No graves: the only human remains are of a person killed in the collapse of Building B (p. 57), not a burial. Explicit absence not coded: p. 63 says the site is 'without water-tight cisterns', but the same source reports silos (pits), so the C2 class is not said to be absent.
